diagnostic_evidence.quote: $G_{3}(\vec x)= G( (y\odot y + z\odot z)^{1/2} \odot v)$
The function $G_{3}$ is locally bounded under \cref{reg1}, and solutions of \cref{cyl} are well defined.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption reg1 only makes G continuously differentiable. The map (y,z) to sqrt(y^2+z^2) is not differentiable at y=z=0, so nabla G_3 need not exist there when v_i[∇G(0)]_i is nonzero. Thus the drift in cyl is not defined on axes, including Cartesian representatives of allowed initial data with U_0,i=0. Local boundedness of G_3 itself does not establish existence or uniqueness for an SDE whose drift is -∇G_3.

If the initial distribution is invariant for the Markov chain generated by the numerical method, so $\rho_0=\pi_\tstep$, we see that
$$
\lim_{\tstep\to 0}
\pi_{\tstep}(P_{T}(\phi))-\pi_\tstep(\phi)
\to 0

issues.failure_explanation: The finite-time theorem is proved for a fixed initial density whose ratio to pi is bounded, with constants depending on that initial law. Here the initial laws pi_Delta t or their truncations vary with Delta t, and no uniform density-ratio, inverse-moment, or strong-error bound is established. Truncating pi_Delta t only makes each ratio finite; it does not make the constants uniform. In addition, invariance concerns the discrete semigroup P_Delta t^k, not the continuous semigroup P_T appearing in the displayed limit, so the replacement requires a missing comparison argument.

failure_location.quote: If $\pi_\tstep$ does not satisfy \cref{reg3}, we may replace $\pi_\tstep$ with  a regularised distribution $\tilde \pi_\tstep$.

issues.overall_effect: The claimed convergence of stationary expectations for every Lipschitz test function is not proved.
issues.title: Invariant-measure convergence applies finite-time convergence non-uniformly to varying initial laws
issues.why_classification: The conclusion may be recoverable with a contained but nontrivial uniformity and semigroup argument; the current pointwise finite-time theorem is insufficient.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Likewise,
the Langevin dynamics are identical to the $\ell_1$ setting, except $\odot$ and the different dimensions of $u$ and $v$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed definition sums squared block norms and is therefore not the group-l1 penalty used by the following radial-mixture identity. Even if the intended penalty is sum_j ||x_bj||, the change x_bj=u_j v_bj contributes u_j^{|b_j|} to the Jacobian, so the augmented density generally has block-size-dependent powers, not merely product_j u_j. Consequently the singular drift and Langevin dynamics are not identical to the scalar-block case.
